question: Should OpenClaw adopt this v1 canonical readiness condition model, activation-scoped plugin provider boundary, and explicit `gateway.readiness` criteria selection as public contracts?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent and well-proven, but merging it commits OpenClaw to new plugin API, configuration, failure, timeout, and compatibility semantics that cannot be chosen safely by automated review.

options.title: Accept the v1 contract
options.body: Approve the required/advisory model, activation-scoped providers, and explicit criteria selection, then complete the RFC lifecycle and review the linked implementation against the accepted text.

options.title: Narrow before acceptance
options.body: Keep the canonical core conditions but revise or defer part of the plugin registration, operator-selection, or projection contract before changing the RFC to accepted.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Leave the RFC open or close it as not planned until maintainers want to own an extensible readiness API and its long-term compatibility obligations.

recommendation.title: Accept the v1 contract
recommendation.body: Approve the required/advisory model, activation-scoped providers, and explicit criteria selection, then complete the RFC lifecycle and review the linked implementation against the accepted text.

likelyOwner.reason: This is an OpenClaw-wide product and public-contract decision spanning Gateway behavior, plugin API, configuration, and release compatibility.
